name: shorter terminal insertion splits an existing edge
input: an extension inserted before its shorter prefix
test:
cache = RadixCache()
cache.insert([1, 2, 3, 4])
cache.insert([1, 2])
assert cache.search([1, 2])
assert cache.search([1, 2, 3, 4])
assert not cache.search([1, 2, 3])
assert cache.prefix_match([1, 2, 3, 4, 5]) == [1, 2, 3, 4]
assert cache.prefix_match([1, 2, 3]) == [1, 2]
assert cache.get_all_sequences() == [[1, 2], [1, 2, 3, 4]]

name: divergent insertions split edges without treating partial prefixes as terminals
input: three sequences sharing prefixes of different lengths
test:
cache = RadixCache()
cache.insert([5, 6, 7])
cache.insert([5, 6, 8])
cache.insert([5, 9])
assert cache.search([5, 6, 7])
assert cache.search([5, 6, 8])
assert cache.search([5, 9])
assert not cache.search([5])
assert not cache.search([5, 6])
assert cache.prefix_match([5, 6]) == []
assert cache.prefix_match([5, 6, 8, 0]) == [5, 6, 8]
assert cache.get_all_sequences() == [[5, 6, 7], [5, 6, 8], [5, 9]]

name: input snapshots, duplicates, and validation have deterministic behavior
input: a caller-mutated sequence plus invalid inputs
test:
cache = RadixCache()
sequence = [9, 1]
cache.insert(sequence)
cache.insert([9, 1])
sequence.append(2)
assert cache.search([9, 1])
assert not cache.search([9, 1, 2])
assert cache.get_all_sequences() == [[9, 1]]
assert cache.prefix_match([]) == []
assert not cache.search([])
for call in (
    lambda: cache.insert((1, 2)),
    lambda: cache.insert([1, True]),
    lambda: cache.search('12'),
    lambda: cache.prefix_match([1, 2.0]),
):
    try:
        call()
        raise AssertionError('expected TypeError')
    except TypeError:
        pass
